stem: A patient asks the pharmacist to dispense part of a new prescription for generic oxymorphone tablets today and return later for the balance. Which limit governs the remainder?

choices.text: Treat it as a patient-requested Schedule II partial fill and dispense any lawful remainder within the applicable 30-day window.
Require a new prescription for every amount left after today's patient-requested partial fill.
Measure the remainder deadline from today's partial-fill date.
Allow the patient to collect the balance from a different pharmacy.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Treat it as a patient-requested Schedule II partial fill and dispense any lawful remainder within the applicable 30-day window.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Apply the 72-hour remainder rule automatically.' would require that the pharmacy, rather than the patient, could not supply the full quantity. The decisive cue appears in 'A patient asks the pharmacist to dispense part of a new prescription for generic oxymorphone tablets today and return later for the balance. Which limit governs the remainder?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Treat it as a patient-requested Schedule II partial fill and dispense any lawful remainder within the applicable 30-day window.': supported by patient request.
choice_analysis.B: 'Apply the 72-hour remainder rule automatically.' would apply only if the pharmacy, rather than the patient, could not supply the full quantity; 'A patient asks the pharmacist to dispense part of a new prescription for generic oxymorphone tablets today and return later for the balance. Which limit governs the remainder?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Require a new prescription for every amount left after today's patient-requested partial fill.' would apply only if the federal and Massachusetts patient-request pathways did not authorize a documented remainder; 'A patient asks the pharmacist to dispense part of a new prescription for generic oxymorphone tablets today and return later for the balance. Which limit governs the remainder?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Measure the remainder deadline from today's partial-fill date.' would apply only if the controlling 30-day period ran from partial dispensing instead of prescription issuance; 'A patient asks the pharmacist to dispense part of a new prescription for generic oxymorphone tablets today and return later for the balance. Which limit governs the remainder?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Allow the patient to collect the balance from a different pharmacy.' would apply only if Massachusetts did not restrict the remainder to the original partially filling pharmacy; 'A patient asks the pharmacist to dispense part of a new prescription for generic oxymorphone tablets today and return later for the balance. Which limit governs the remainder?' states otherwise.

related_facts: Generic oxymorphone products are opioid analgesics used for severe pain and remain federal and Massachusetts Schedule II. OPANA and OPANA ER are discontinued brand products and are not presented here as current brands.

A Schedule II prescription may be partially filled at the patient or prescriber request when state law permits, with the remaining portion dispensed no later than 30 days after the prescription was written unless a shorter applicable limit controls.
